user.title: HUAWEI ID sign-in in a browser
user.description:
No Huawei Health app is involved: the cloud mints the token pair after an ordinary HUAWEI ID sign-in in a browser. Only the consent step is manual, everything else the integration does itself.

**Step 1. Open the sign-in page in a normal browser** (Chrome, Firefox, whatever you use):

[{authorize_url}]({authorize_url})

**Step 2. Switch the browser into mobile device mode.** The *Allow* button on the consent page responds to touch only — a mouse click does nothing.

1. Press **F12** (or **Ctrl+Shift+I**, on macOS **Cmd+Option+I**) to open DevTools.
2. Press **Ctrl+Shift+M** (on macOS **Cmd+Shift+M**) — that is the *Toggle device toolbar* button in the top-left corner of the DevTools panel.
3. In the bar that appears, pick a device such as **iPhone 12 Pro** or **Pixel 7** and press **Reload** (the round arrow in the same bar).
4. The page reloads with the mobile layout: scroll to the bottom and press **Allow** — the cursor now behaves like a finger.

**Step 3. Come back here** and paste the address the browser stopped on in the next step.

Full instructions, click by click: {docs}

code.title: Paste the address that carries the code
code.description:
**Where the code lives.** After you press *Allow* the browser tries to open a link like `hms://redirect_url?code=...` and cannot: no application on this computer registers that scheme. Chrome says so in the console, and that line is what is needed:

```
Failed to launch 'hms://redirect_url?code=EQFEAQNaOARz0K1p%2BmR7sT4uVwXyZ0...%3D%3D&state=9f2c1ab7' because the scheme does not have a registered handler.
```

1. In DevTools open the **Console** tab (F12 → Console).
2. Find the line starting with `Failed to launch 'hms://redirect_url?code=`.
3. Copy the whole line — the `Failed to launch` and `because the scheme...` text around it is fine, the integration throws it away. The `hms://redirect_url?code=...` address from the address bar works too.
4. Paste it below and press **Submit**.

The code is single-use and lives a few minutes. If it is refused, open the sign-in page from step 1 again and repeat the whole procedure.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign-in required again
reauth_confirm.description:
The session of **{account}** can no longer be refreshed: the refresh token expired (Huawei issues it for 180 days) or was revoked by a sign-out.

Nothing has to be deleted: sign in again in the browser and the integration will put the new tokens into this same entry — history and sensor settings stay intact.

**Step 1.** Open the sign-in page: [{authorize_url}]({authorize_url})

**Step 2.** Turn on mobile device mode in DevTools (**F12**, then **Ctrl+Shift+M**), otherwise the *Allow* button will not react to the mouse.

**Step 3.** Copy the `Failed to launch 'hms://redirect_url?code=...'` line from DevTools → Console and paste it in the next step.

Details: {docs}

abort.already_configured: This HUAWEI ID account is already set up.
abort.reauth_successful: Done: tokens refreshed and the account reloaded.
abort.unsupported_import: YAML configuration is not supported: add the account under Integrations.

error.no_code: No code in that field: paste an address like hms://redirect_url?code=... from the browser console.
error.invalid_code: Huawei refused the code: already used, expired, or another account signed in. Open the sign-in page again and repeat.
error.cannot_connect: The Huawei cloud could not be reached. Check the network and try again.
error.unknown: Unknown error. See the Home Assistant log for details.

init.title: Account settings
init.description: Every account is configured on its own. Changes are applied without restarting Home Assistant.

data.history_days: Days of daily data to keep
data.workout_days: How many days back to look for workouts
data.enable_health_metrics: Poll heart rate, sleep and stress (getHealthStat)
data.device_code: deviceCode of one device (0 = whole account)

data_description.update_interval: Below 5 minutes is pointless: the app cloud only moves when a watch or phone syncs.
data_description.history_days: Affects the daily sensors; up to 30 days still costs a single request.
data_description.workout_days: Workouts are read in 10-day windows (a hard cloud limit), so 30 days is three requests.
data_description.device_code: /profile/device/getBindDevice lists the codes. Setting a watch's code restricts the daily totals to that device.
data_description.enable_workouts: Turn off if you never record workouts: it drops the slowest request.
data_description.enable_health_metrics: Turn off if no device measures heart rate or sleep.
